# v0.27.0-rc1 — summary quality: fleet-proven defaults, summaries that see the middle, stemmed recall

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md) at this tag: the all-tools live matrix bound to `hermes-lcm-x v0.27.0 (15 tools)`
(A); a P0/P1 sweep of the `v0.26.2`→rc diff, including upgrade from and rollback to v0.26.2 (B); a 30+ turn live host
soak with a committed compaction, 0 loss, 0 duplicates, 0 truncated level-3 nodes (C); the scorecard: recall flips
vs the previous GA, facts kept in long sessions, the OFF QA rows and latency (gauntlet cells max ≤ 145 s), each against a pre-declared bar (D, new);
and 24 h or more on the reference agent with field-window counters (p90 ≤ 60 s, max ≤ 120 s).

GA follows only when the receipts are green. The GA tree is this tree plus the `v0.27.0` release-notes file.

Minor release on top of `v0.26.2`. It includes the `v0.26.1` and `v0.26.2` fixes. Theme: **summary quality**, built as a
four-layer compaction architecture:
1. **Old tool output goes first.** Large outputs are externalized and replayed as stubs that name the read-back call.
2. **Summaries.** DAG summaries now see the middle of long messages.
3. **Deterministic re-insertion.** The objective, the LCM note and the user's current request survive compaction verbatim.
4. **Lossless, searchable history.** Every raw row stays in the store; recall is stemmed, and with embeddings on it
   embeds new work in the background.

**The defaults now match the configuration the managed deployment has run on every profile for weeks.** This is the
one change most users will notice: compaction starts later (at 75% of the window instead of 35%), and old tool output
is externalized by default. To keep the old behaviour, set the keys listed under **Upgrade**.

- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged. Two dormant tools
  are no longer advertised under defaults (see #1013 part 2).
- No new `LCM_*` setting except `LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR` (default on, embeddings-on only) and `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE`
  (default unchanged).
- **Store:** `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 5. The stemmed full-text index is a droppable side table that a background backfill
  builds; doctor and status report it, and `/lcm doctor repair apply` re-creates it.
- No change below deletes a stored raw row.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Upgrade

**Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required** (#1080). `plugin.yaml` now declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.3"`, the same floor
as the catalog entry. On Hermes 0.21.2 or older, Hermes skips the plugin and uses its built-in compressor, and the
existing LCM-X database is left untouched. Upgrade Hermes before upgrading the plugin. The reliability nightly tests the
floor host, 0.21.3.

**Hermes 0.21.5 or newer is recommended.** On 0.21.3 and 0.21.4, a compaction right after a tool call can leave the turn
un-anchored, and Hermes sends its own "tool did not complete" notices in place of that turn's results. The results stay
stored and recall finds them; 0.21.5 fixed it upstream, and the nightly licenses this behaviour on the floor host (#1094).

**New defaults** (#1013). Each is the value the managed profiles already run:

| Setting | v0.26.x | v0.27.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` | `0.35` | `0.75` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT` | `32` | `24` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` | `0` (no cap) | `24000` |
| `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS` | `20000` | `8000` |
| `LCM_THRESHOLD_FULL_SWEEP_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_ACTIVE_REPLAY_STUBBING_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_TEMPORAL_ROLLUPS_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |

- Thresholds are unchanged: the first-sight stub threshold stays 10,000 tokens.
- A threshold inherited from Hermes `compression.threshold` is raised to at least `0.75`. A bare Hermes install seeds
  `0.50`, so it now compacts at `0.75`; `/lcm status` shows the source `config_yaml:compression.threshold(floored)` with
  a config warning. Set `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` or `lcm.context_threshold` to go lower; neither is floored.
- `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=0` now means no fresh tail, whatever `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` is.
- Embeddings stay off by default. Managed deployments turn on the local provider through their own keys.

**Rollback:** to `v0.26.2`, plugin only, unless a survival fit on this store projected rows or its projection count is
unknown. In that case a plugin-only rollback must target `v0.27.0` or later. For an older target, stop Hermes and move
the database file (with its `-wal` and `-shm` companions) aside first; otherwise a cold resume stores the projected rows
again. `/lcm doctor` names the floor for each store (#919, #966).

## Changes since v0.26.2

### Defaults and request size
- **#1013 parts A–C: defaults = the deployed configuration** (table above).
- **#1013 part 2 (#1017): dormant tools hidden.** Under defaults, `lcm_query_state` and `lcm_retrieve` are no longer
  advertised until `LCM_ASSERTIONS_ENABLED` / `LCM_ADAPTIVE_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED` is on. That saves 5,534 serialized JSON
  bytes per request (about 1,384 tokens). The manifest still declares all 15 tools.
- **#1055: the user/assistant inline floor follows the window.** User and assistant text is externalized only above the
  larger of 25,000 tokens and a tenth of the session's window, so long-window sessions keep long messages inline. With
  an unknown window the v0.26.2 floor applies. Tool output and media keep the configured threshold.

### Layer 1 — tool output
- **#1075:** `/lcm backup` and `/lcm rotate apply` name the externalized-payload directory, with its file count and
  size, to copy alongside a snapshot moved to another host.

### Layer 2 — summaries
- **#611: summaries see the middle of long messages.** A shared input budget with a legacy retention floor replaces the
  fixed head/tail clip. Measured middle-fact retention: 0/72 → 42/72 on the same material.
- **#899, #947:** a clipped long message, or a leaf whose summariser input was clipped, is summarised and never stored
  as a verbatim level-3 leaf.
- **#930, #954, #977: a bounded summary prefix.** With a known window the prefix is bounded by default, keeping the
  newest summaries without deleting DAG nodes. A routine sweep condenses the shallowest eligible depth, so older
  summaries keep their detail; the heaviest depth goes first only under pressure.
- **#904, #922:** hidden-only compaction leaves the host list unchanged when nothing shrinks; a leaf that only repeats
  the preserved objective is skipped.
- **#1012:** a summariser content-filter rejection of one chunk no longer opens the summary route's circuit; that chunk
  gets the deterministic level-3 leaf and its rows stay stored. The survival fit reserves the largest host overhead seen,
  so the host's turn-start preflight no longer fails a request that fits.
- **#1099:** a summary call cut at the foreground budget's deadline after outliving its configured timeout no longer
  counts as a route failure. Hosts that publish that deadline, and whose timeout is a no-progress window (the Codex
  Responses route), no longer open the summary circuit on a slow but live summary.

### Layer 3 — what survives compaction verbatim
- **#921, #958, #1048: the user's objective.** A second assembly in the same turn keeps it; a newer request merged onto
  it survives on its own under a cap; the budget reserves the stubs the final sanitizer adds, so unanswered tool calls
  no longer push the objective out.
- **#900, #953: the LCM note reaches the model on Hermes** as a plugin system-prompt section, only in sessions LCM
  manages, naming only enabled tools, and never in auxiliary or bypass sessions.
- **#998:** the note names `lcm_recall` first for facts from earlier sessions, and says `lcm_grep` searches this session
  by default. Every agent sees this prompt change.
- **#659: the user carry packet moves to v0.27.1.** The end-to-end check on a real host was inconclusive. Accuracy was
  +2 pt (95% interval −5 to +9 pt); the bar needs a lower bound above −5 pt. The other five guards held: user-evidence
  questions, fail-closed turns, tokens per correct answer (lower with the packet), p90 wall, and duplicates. The mechanism
  check over 8 seeds was inconclusive too: user facts −1.1 pt (interval −8.2 to +6.7), all facts +1.2 pt.

### Layer 4 — recall
- **#1021, #1035: stemmed full-text recall.** `lcm_recall`'s full-text arm ranks over a porter-stemmed copy of message
  content once its backfill completes. On the LongMemEval-M retrieval set (500 questions, 470 scored), R@10 .847 → .873
  (paired, p = .0009). Cost: about 22% more database size, about 0.2 ms per message write, about 72 ms more at the
  median on the full-text arm. `lcm_grep` and the other paths keep exact and prefix matching.
- **#1015: `lcm_grep` honours the FTS5 operators its schema advertises** (`OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR`, `term*`); a rejected
  query retries in the old form, and a multi-term query with no hits retries once as any-term.
- **#1014, #1063: embeddings keep up by themselves.** With embeddings on, a bounded background pass embeds new leaf
  summaries (and, with FastEmbed or a loopback Ollama, new message chunks). With FastEmbed the pass registers the
  embedding profile itself and never downloads a model. FastEmbed uses 2 threads and honours `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`.
- **#995, #1008: event time.** `lcm_recall` hits carry `event_time` when the host recorded one; proactive recall dates
  a memory by event time and labels LCM's write time `stored`.
- **#950:** with embeddings on, the full-text arm's best match is kept in the ranked window (`LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR`).
- **#1047:** the LIKE fallback fetches its candidate window in one query (a 767K-message CJK store took 146 s before).

### Identity, durability and operations
- **#1000:** a summary carrier a survival fit re-forms around a kept user row is no longer stored again as a new row.
- **#959:** a survival projection is recognised on a cold resume even when its tool-call arguments quote survival marks.
- **#852:** `/lcm` refuses every subcommand when the session and engine profiles differ.
- **#903:** `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE` configures SQLite mapped reads (default unchanged); use `0` on SD-card hosts.
- **#1084 (#1088):** `/lcm doctor` reports the linked SQLite version and whether it has SQLite's WAL-reset bug, and LCM-X
  logs one warning per process on an affected SQLite. No behaviour change.
- **#1080 (Hermes catalog review):** the not-active marker moves under `plugin-data/hermes-lcm-x/`; `fastembed` is
  bounded to `>=0.8.0,<1.0`; the plugin no longer writes the host's private hook table when `register_hook` is missing.

## Bench and instruments (no runtime change)
- Track S: isolated Codex-arm homes (#951), cap-cut replies retried not scored (#974), per-file digest admission and
  paired metrics (#946, #948). Eval-2: v4 material with lifecycle probes, manifest-bound admission, one pinned head per
  arm; incomplete pairs make a verdict INCONCLUSIVE (#1064, #1079, #1087). Reliability: B1/B2 resolve externalized rows (#1056).

## Qualification
- **Independent review.** Every product PR since `v0.26.0` (49, plus #1101) had a review of its merged head by a model
  session other than its author (the Codex connector on every PR; Claude also reviewed most Codex-written lanes), or only
  text changed after it. Two exceptions: #1019's head review arrived after merge (findings dispositioned, #1103), and
  #1081's last commit only added `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.3"`, which the nightly's floor host exercises.
- Full suite, the CI way: 7,523 passed, 108 skipped, 19 xfailed, 0 failed on Python 3.11–3.14 (run 38134944460); lint clean.
- The rollback readers in CI now include `v0.26.2`, against a store this candidate wrote, including writes under the
  stemmed-index triggers and the moved not-active marker (#1100). The reliability nightly passed
  its gate on all 5 hosts at the rc base `8bb7b70a` (run 38130276087; 103 cells each, 0 gating).
- The gauntlet runs at the `v0.27.0-rc1` tag; its receipts are what the GA notes link.

## Known follow-ups
- **#1096:** with a slow summariser, a call can run to the 120 s foreground bound and the pass then writes no leaf.
  v0.27.1 measures, then bounds, the summary output length per route. (v0.27.1)
- **#1068:** Hermes' native Responses compaction (`compression.codex_responses_native`) reads LCM-X's threshold and can
  fire before it. Keep it off with LCM-X until Hermes gates native compaction per context engine. (v0.28.0)
- **#1086:** a shutdown does not wait for background work such as rollups and embedding passes. (v0.28.0)
- **#1066:** an identifier index after compaction (layer 3), shipped only if Eval-2 measures it as not hurting. (v0.28.0)
- **#1083:** below the plugin API floor (no `register_hook`), withhold the context engine instead of running without
  per-turn ingest. Until then the plugin logs one warning, and `plugin.yaml` declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.3"`.
  (v0.28.0)
- **#1085:** what an affected SQLite (the WAL-reset bug) should change: follow the host's journal policy or serialize
  LCM's writers, decided with a stress measurement. (v0.28.0)

## Benchmark boundary
- Measured in this release: stemmed recall (R@10 .847 → .873, #1035) and middle-of-message retention (0/72 → 42/72, #611).
  The Phase D scorecard (recall flips, facts kept, OFF QA rows, latency) runs at this tag; the GA notes report its rows.
